Let \( a_0, a_1, a_2, \ldots \) be the unique sequence of nonnegative integers less than 397 with \( a_0 = 1 \) and

\[ a_{n+1}(a_n + 1)^2 \equiv a_n \pmod{397} \]

for all nonnegative integers \( n \). Given that \( a_{2026} = 9 \), compute the remainder when \( a_0 + a_1 + \cdots + a_{2026} \) is divided by 397.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
Let all congruences be taken modulo \(397\). Since \(a_0=1\) and \(a_{2026}=9\), the terms involved are nonzero, so we may define

\[
b_n \equiv a_n^{-1}.
\]

From

\[
a_{n+1}(a_n+1)^2 \equiv a_n,
\]

we get

\[
a_{n+1} \equiv \frac{a_n}{(a_n+1)^2}.
\]

Taking inverses,

\[
b_{n+1} \equiv a_n^{-1}(a_n+1)^2
= a_n + 2 + a_n^{-1}
= a_n+2+b_n.
\]

Thus

\[
a_n \equiv b_{n+1}-b_n-2.
\]

Summing from \(n=0\) to \(2026\),

\[
\sum_{n=0}^{2026} a_n
\equiv (b_{2027}-b_0)-2\cdot 2027.
\]

Now \(b_0=a_0^{-1}=1\). Also \(a_{2026}=9\), so

\[
b_{2026}\equiv 9^{-1}.
\]

Since \(9\cdot 44\equiv -1 \pmod{397}\), we have

\[
9^{-1}\equiv -44\equiv 353 \pmod{397}.
\]

Then

\[
b_{2027}\equiv b_{2026}+a_{2026}+2
\equiv 353+9+2=364.
\]

Therefore

\[
\sum_{n=0}^{2026} a_n
\equiv 364-1-2(2027)
=363-4054
\equiv -3691
\equiv 279 \pmod{397}.
\]

\[
\boxed{279}
\]
